docs(console): describe the eight methods Console has, not the fourteen it doesn't (rich-docs-site-13t.4) (#84)

* docs(console): describe the eight methods Console has, not the fourteen it doesn't (rich-docs-site-13t.4)

The ticket named `logLocals`. The page carried twenty-two false claims.

`Console`'s real surface is eight methods: print, log, rule, printJson,
beginCapture, endCapture, exportText, exportHtml. The page documented six
members that do not exist — `out`, `status`, `input`, `screen`, `pager`, and a
static `Console.capture()` — across five sections and two blocks that declared
`const console` twice, which would be a SyntaxError if run.

Three of those six are real capabilities documented on the wrong object. This
port moved several of Python Rich's Console methods to standalone classes, and
the docs were never told, so `status`, `input` and `screen` redirect to
`Status`, `Prompt` and `Live` rather than being deleted. `out` and `pager` have
no implementation anywhere and are gone.

The rest could not have been caught by any type checker, because every one of
them type-checks clean:

- `logLocals` is not configuration. `print()` sniffs its last argument for known
  option keys, so an unrecognized options object is demoted to a value to print,
  stringified to `[object Object]`, and eaten by the markup parser. It prints
  nothing — not, as the ticket assumed, a literal object.
- Printing or logging a plain object hits that same swallow and yields a blank
  line. The page claimed both were pretty-printed.
- `log()` adds a timestamp and nothing else; there is no location column.
- `rule()` does not parse markup in its title.
- `printJson` re-indents but does not colorize, while `print()` of the same
  string does.
- `crop`, `justify: "left"`, `justify: "full"` and `overflow: "ignore"` are
  accepted and inert.
- `NO_COLOR` strips bold along with colour, contradicting the page.
- The colour-system table listed two specs that throw, omitted the two that
  work, and gave the Windows palette as 8 colours where it has 16.

Every claim above was verified by executing it against a width-pinned console
and capturing stdout, and every code block on the page now type-checks against
`src/`.

Filed rather than fixed here: rich-console-nac (four inert PrintOptions),
rich-console-8lg (printJson's sortKeys silently no-ops via a cast to the
replacer parameter, and its missing highlighting), rich-docs-site-dl4
(docs/live.md documents `screen:`/`live.run()`/`new Table("a","b")`, none of
which exist — and console.md now links there).

* docs(console): an object's keys decide whether print takes it as data or options

Two corrections from review, both verified by execution.

The colour-spec claim was generalized from two samples. `STRING_TO_DEPTH` in
`src/core/color.ts` is one table serving configuration and detection both, so
`resolveColorSystem` accepts every FORCE_COLOR value and every terminal
identifier detection knows: `{ colorSystem: "vscode" }` silently means
truecolor, `"true"` means ansi, `"0"` means none. Only strings outside the whole
table throw. The page said any string but the five throws.

`log()`'s trailing argument is not simply a value. It forwards to `print()`,
which sniffs the last argument for the nine `PrintOptions` names, so whether an
object is data or configuration depends on its keys. `end` is one of the nine
and it sets the line terminator, which makes the worst case visible rather than
silent: `console.log("range", { end: "2024" })` emits `range2024` with no
newline. The page asserted a trailing object is always printed as a value.

Both are cases where the type checker sees nothing wrong, which is why neither
turned up in the per-block tsc pass.

* docs(console): Console is the usual way out, not the only one

renderToString is exported from the main barrel and renders any Renderable to
ANSI with no Console constructed — a designed seam, per src/core/render.ts's
"no `Console` and no writes to stdout". Saying anything that draws goes through
a Console contradicted docs/protocol.md, which documents that path.

This replaces an overstatement introduced earlier in this branch while fixing a
wider one: narrowing "every feature passes through Console" to drawing was
still wrong, because drawing is exactly what renderToString does.

* docs(console): nothing detects the Windows palette, so don't imply it does

detectColorSystem has no branch returning ColorDepth.WINDOWS, and src/ contains
no win32 or process.platform check at all. The page called it "a detection
result rather than something you ask for", which promised a reader that legacy
Windows terminals get this palette automatically. They never do — the enum value
is the only path to it.

The phrase came from color.ts's "WINDOWS is a detection result (max enum value),
not a downgrade target", which is fair in its own context: it explains why the
WINDOWS case in the downgrade switch is unreachable. Read as a claim about
detection it is not, and that is the reading the page shipped.
